title_en: Shekou District Environmental Monitoring Station of Shenzhen v. Hong Kong Kaida Enterprise Co., Ltd. — environmental pollution dispute
keywords_en: Administrative; Environmental pollution liability dispute; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Guangdong Province; State organ; Foreign-invested enterprise; Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation); Noise pollution control; Waste gas emission control; Obligation to undertake remediation within a time limit; Bearing of pollution remediation costs; In favor of the plaintiff; Plastic toy manufacturing; Excessive noise; Emission of malodorous gases; Failure to perform remediation within the time limit; Who pollutes, who treats
full_text_en:
Shekou District Environmental Monitoring Station of Shenzhen City v. Hong Kong Kaida Enterprise Co., Ltd. — environmental pollution case

Plaintiff: Shekou District Environmental Monitoring Station of Shenzhen City (hereinafter referred to as the "Monitoring Station").

Defendant: Hong Kong Kaida Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Kaida").

In September 1981, the Defendant Kaida signed an agreement with the Shenzhen Special Zone Merchants Bureau, establishing a wholly-owned factory in the Shekou Industrial Zone to produce various plastic toys, with an investment of USD 16 million and a workforce of 1,200 employees. Its products were sold well on the international market. In February 1982, after the company commenced formal production, the injection molding workshop emitted foul-smelling and toxic gases without treatment, directly discharging them into the atmosphere, causing throat and nasal irritation and breathing difficulties. Meanwhile, the noise from the machinery was deafening and caused irritation. In response, nearby enterprises, institutions, government agencies, and residents reported to the Monitoring Station, requesting serious action by the government.

Based on the strong demands of the public, starting from early May 1983, the Plaintiff Monitoring Station repeatedly urged the Defendant to control the pollution. It successively engaged experts, professors, and technical personnel from relevant scientific research institutions in Guangzhou to conduct multiple surveys at Kaida, providing remediation plans and assisting in pollution control, but the Defendant did not adopt any of them. On October 22, 1983, the Plaintiff issued a notice to the Defendant requiring pollution control within a specified time limit. In response, the Defendant still did not take effective measures. Under these circumstances, on December 27 of the same year, the Plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, requesting that the Defendant thoroughly control the aforementioned noise and exhaust gas to meet national standards, and pay the relevant expenses for engaging environmental protection technical personnel to conduct surveys.

The Defendant argued in its defense: Before October 22, 1983, the Plaintiff had never provided our company with legally effective scientific appraisal materials concerning environmental pollution or relevant national standards, yet accused our company of producing noise and emitting foul odors in production, which was perplexing; requiring our company to spend USD 40,000 to install a "filtering device" was even harder to accept; it was truly impossible for us to complete pollution control by December 25, 1983 as demanded by the Plaintiff, and the injection molding workshop had already ceased production as required within the time limit.

After accepting the case, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court conducted extensive investigations and found:

(1) The noise issue: According to national standards, when workers are exposed to noise for eight hours per working day, the permissible level is 85 decibels; in industrial concentrated areas, the daytime noise level is 65 decibels. However, the daily working hours of workers in Kaida's injection molding workshop exceeded eight hours, with a maximum noise value of 106 decibels and a minimum of 91 decibels; the daytime noise from the air compressor room was 87 decibels, all greatly exceeding national standards.

(2) The exhaust gas issue: The physical and chemical properties of the raw materials used in Kaida's injection molding workshop had never been provided to the Plaintiff. It was only after the Plaintiff engaged technical personnel to collect samples at the production site and perform spectral qualitative analysis that it was discovered that the main components of the raw materials were polyvinyl chloride (PVC) mixed with a large amount of dioctyl phthalate (DOP) plasticizer, which emitted foul-smelling gases during heating and molding. The exhaust gases from 36 injection molding machines were emitted into the atmosphere without treatment, causing air pollution. In January 1984, after the lawsuit began, the Defendant only then provided the Plaintiff with foreign language materials on the plasticizer composition, which after translation proved that the plasticizer belonged to the fatty acid class of malodorous groups.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held in its consideration: Article 6 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) provides: "All enterprises and institutions, in their site selection, design, construction, and production, must fully take into account the prevention of environmental pollution and damage. When undertaking new construction, renovation, or expansion projects, an environmental impact report must be submitted, and design may only proceed after review and approval by the environmental protection department and other relevant departments. The facilities for preventing pollution and other public hazards must be designed, constructed, and put into operation simultaneously with the main project. The discharge of all harmful substances must comply with the standards prescribed by the state. Units that have already caused environmental pollution and other public hazards shall, in accordance with the principle of 'the polluter controls,' formulate plans and actively carry out control." However, during the factory construction and production process, the Defendant not only failed to submit an environmental impact report to the environmental protection department or declare the chemical composition of the production raw materials, but also demanded that the environmental protection department identify the source of the foul odor and provide scientific data, which was entirely unreasonable. After the Plaintiff lawfully issued a notice requiring the Defendant to control pollution within a specified time limit, although the Defendant stopped production on December 24, 1983 (Christmas Eve), it resumed production from January 3 to 13, 1984, continuing to discharge pollutants. The Defendant's above actions were illegal.

Accordingly, on July 14, 1984, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Articles 6, 16, and 32 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), rendered the following judgment:

1. The Defendant shall, by October 31, 1984, comprehensively control the noise and foul odor in the injection molding workshop to meet the standards prescribed by the state.

2. The Defendant, having failed to take effective measures to actively carry out pollution control in response to the Plaintiff's lawful notice requiring pollution control within a specified time limit, and instead continuing production and discharge of pollutants, is fined HKD 20,000 for such illegal conduct, to be turned over to the state treasury.

3. The expenses of RMB 810 incurred by the Plaintiff for engaging relevant technical personnel to conduct tests and surveys at the Defendant's factory on multiple occasions shall be borne by the Defendant.

4. The litigation costs of this case, HKD 1,740, shall be borne by the Defendant.

After the judgment was pronounced, the Defendant accepted the judgment.

At its 232nd meeting on August 17, 1985, the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 11, Paragraph 1 of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, in summarizing trial experience, held that the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, in adjudicating this case, strictly implemented the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), rendered a correct judgment, restrained the act of environmental pollution, and protected the people's health.
